name: SendFox
tagline: Simple email broadcasts, automations, landing pages, and Smart campaigns

pricing.notes: The pricing model is not safely comparable as one fixed monthly USD amount. Review the official source before publication.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 1,000 contacts, 3,000 sends/month, 1 smart page, 1 form, 1 automation, no API, no MCP, branding.

tiers.name: Lifetime License
tiers.limits: 5,000 contacts, 300,000 lifetime sends, unlimited automations/smart pages/forms, full API.
tiers.notes: $29 one-time lifetime license; footer remains unless Pro.

tiers.name: Pro 5K
tiers.limits: 5,000 contacts, 100,000 sends/month, white label, MCP, VIP sending IP, paid newsletters, HTML editor.

tiers.name: Pro 25K
tiers.limits: 25,000 contacts; higher send/contact tier of Pro.

pricing.freeTierCaps: $0; 1,000 contacts, 3,000 sends/month, 1 smart page, 1 form, 1 automation, branding, no API/MCP.
pricing.billingTerms: free + one-time lifetime license + monthly Pro; annual Pro gives 2 months free
pricing.hiddenCosts: Lifetime plan has 300,000 lifetime sends and keeps footer; Pro price grows with contact tier.

verdictSummary: The visible creator email marketing loop is buildable, but a credible replacement needs more than the first screen. SendFox earns its keep through deliverability, reputation, network, so expect a weekend or multi-day build and a narrower personal scope.
coreLoopDIY: Build a small creator email marketing editor and subscriber database that exports clean HTML and sends only through a reputable user-supplied email provider.
replacementScope: narrow personal or very small-team substitute
requirements: transactional or bulk email provider key in .env
whatYouLose: sender reputation, deliverability, and suppression handling
whyPeopleStillPay: SendFox: The editor is trivial compared with inbox placement, compliance, reputation, unsubscribe handling, analytics, and audience growth infrastructure.
ongoingBurden: Own consent records, suppression lists, bounces, complaints, DNS, templates, accessibility, segmentation, and privacy requests.

priorArt.name: listmonk
priorArt.desc: High-performance self-hosted newsletter and mailing-list manager.

alternatives.name: Brevo Free
alternatives.desc: Campaigns, forms and automation with a 300-message daily speed governor.

facts.dataFormat: Contacts, campaigns, consent records, and message events live in Brevo's cloud; contacts can be exported as CSV.
facts.gapVsPaid: Brevo Free supplies campaigns, forms, and automation, but the 300-message daily governor and lack of SendFox-style automatic content campaigns are meaningful downgrades.
facts.setupBlocker: Authenticating a custom sending domain requires adding DNS records.

alternatives.name: EmailOctopus Free
alternatives.desc: Simple broadcasts, forms and three short automations; enough for a modest creator list.

facts.dataFormat: Lists, campaigns, automations, and reporting data live in EmailOctopus' cloud; contacts and reports can be exported as CSV.
facts.gapVsPaid: EmailOctopus Free handles broadcasts and forms, but three short automations and one form are less flexible than SendFox's creator workflow.
facts.setupBlocker: You must verify a sender address or domain; DNS authentication is the first technical step.

alternatives.name: Kit Free
alternatives.desc: Unlimited sends, landing pages and one sequence for 10,000 subscribers; creator features are stronger.

facts.dataFormat: Subscribers, tags, forms, broadcasts, sequences, purchases, and analytics live in Kit's cloud; subscriber and chart data export as CSV.
facts.gapVsPaid: Kit Free is stronger for creator forms and newsletters, but its free sequence/automation limits and lack of SendFox's Smart Campaign content recycling remain tradeoffs.
facts.setupBlocker: There is no software install, but custom-domain sending requires DNS authentication and the free plan keeps one Kit-managed recommendation slot.

alternatives.name: Mautic
alternatives.desc: Broadcasts and automations with no contact cap; the server stack is wildly less simple.

alternatives.name: Sender Free
alternatives.desc: Broadcasts, landing pages and unlimited workflows in a generous free plan; Smart campaigns become ordinary automations.

facts.dataFormat: Subscribers, campaigns, automations, and engagement events live in Sender's cloud; subscriber data can be exported.
facts.gapVsPaid: Sender Free provides generous broadcasts, pages, and workflows, but it has no equivalent to SendFox's automatic Smart Campaign content curation.
facts.setupBlocker: A custom sending domain must be verified with DNS records for reliable delivery.

notes: Useful boundary case: the first 60 percent of SendFox is approachable, but operating the last 40 percent is the real subscription.
prompt:
Build a deliberately narrow personal substitute for SendFox, not a full clone.
Use exactly this stack: Next.js 15 + TypeScript + PostgreSQL.
Primary job: Build a small creator email marketing editor and subscriber database that exports clean HTML and sends only through a reputable user-supplied email provider.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: payments, recommendations, and audience network; sender reputation, deliverability, and suppression handling; sender reputation and deliverability operations.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
